claim: On 2026-07-22 AWS Organizations raised the number of resource control policies (RCPs) per organization to 2,000, doubling the previous limit of 1,000; existing organizations get the higher limit automatically.
question: When did the RCP quota per organization change, and from what to what?

evidence.quote: AWS Organizations now supports up to 2,000 resource control policies (RCPs) per organization, doubling the previous limit of 1,000.
No action is required — existing organizations automatically have access to the higher limit.

note: d042, d132. GA after 2026-07-15: not examinable yet (RULINGS rule 7). The current quota page already lists Resource control policies: 2000 (organizations-policies-per-organization).

claim: Since 2026-07-10, when you create a new organization in the AWS Organizations console, Organizations automatically applies SCPs that prevent member accounts from leaving the organization or closing themselves; you can modify or disable these settings at any time.
question: What security controls does AWS Organizations apply by default to a new organization created in the console, and since when?

values.display: prevent member accounts from leaving the organization
values.spoken: prevent member accounts from leaving the organization

qualifiers.scope: new organizations created in the AWS Organizations console
qualifiers.condition: available in US East (N. Virginia), AWS GovCloud (US) and China Regions

evidence.quote: When you create a new organization using the AWS Organizations console, the service automatically applies service control policies (SCPs) that prevent member accounts from leaving the organization or closing themselves.
You maintain full control to modify or disable these settings at any time.

note: d132. GA after 2026-07-15: not examinable yet. Older questions assume a new organization has only FullAWSAccess attached.

claim: On 2025-11-19 AWS Organizations added direct account transfers: an account can move to a different organization without first being removed from its current organization, which ends the previous requirement for the account to temporarily operate as a standalone account.
question: When did AWS Organizations allow an account to move directly from one organization to another, and what step did that remove?

values.display: temporarily operate as a standalone account
values.spoken: temporarily operate as a standalone account

evidence.quote: Allowing direct transfers of accounts between organizations eliminates the previous requirement for the account to temporarily operate as a standalone account.
AWS Organizations now provides customers the ability to directly transfer an account to a different organization without first having to remove the account from their current organization.

changed.was: temporarily operate as a standalone account

note: d014. Older exam questions assume leave the organization, become standalone, then accept the new invitation.

claim: To migrate an account to another organization, the new organization sends an invitation and the account accepts it; the account does not need to leave its current organization or operate as a standalone account first. Before 2025-11-19 the account had to temporarily operate as a standalone account.
question: Must an account leave its organization and become standalone before it can join another organization?

values.display: doesn't need to leave its current organization
values.spoken: does not need to leave its current organization

evidence.quote: With direct account transfer, you migrate an account by having the new organization send an invitation and the migrating account accept it. The account doesn't need to leave its current organization or operate as a standalone account first.
Allowing direct transfers of accounts between organizations eliminates the previous requirement for the account to temporarily operate as a standalone account.

changed.was: temporarily operate as a standalone account

claim: To migrate an account to a new organization, you must wait at least 7 days after that organization was created.
question: How old must an organization be before an account can be migrated into it?

evidence.quote: To migrate an account to a new organization, you must wait until at least seven days after the organization was created.

claim: To migrate an account that was created in an organization, you must wait at least 4 days after the account was created; invited accounts are not subject to this waiting period.
question: How long after creation can an account created in an organization be migrated to another organization?

qualifiers.scope: per account created in an organization

evidence.quote: To migrate an account that you created in an organization, you must wait until at least four days after the account was created. Invited accounts are not subject to this waiting period.

claim: You cannot migrate a closed or suspended account to another organization.
question: Can a closed or suspended account be migrated to another organization?

values.display: cannot migrate a closed or suspended account
values.spoken: cannot migrate a closed or suspended account

evidence.quote: You cannot migrate a closed or suspended account.

claim: A closed member account shows a CLOSED label in the AWS Organizations console for up to 90 days after the closure date; after 90 days it is permanently closed and no longer displayed, and removal from the organization can take a few more days.
question: How long after closure does a closed member account stay visible in the organization before it is permanently closed?

evidence.quote: After 90 days, the member account will be permanently closed and will no longer be displayed in the AWS Organizations console. Please note that it may take a few days for the account to be removed from the organization after permanent closure.
Any member account that you close will display a `CLOSED` label next to its account name in the AWS Organizations console for up to 90 days after the original closure date.

claim: After you close an AWS account, you can reopen it within 90 days from the day you closed it; this is the post-closure period, after which AWS permanently closes the account.
question: For how long after closing an AWS account can you reopen it?

evidence.quote: After you've closed it, you can reopen it within 90 days from the day you closed the account. The period between the day you closed the account and when AWS permanently closes the account is referred to as the [post-closure period](#post-closure-period).

claim: Each invitation to join an organization must be answered within 15 days, or it expires.
question: How long does an account have to accept an invitation to join an organization?

evidence.quote: Each invitation must be responded to within 15 days, or it expires.

note: d015. The handshake table on the quota page says the same (Invitation to join an organization | 15 days).

claim: AWS Organizations is a global service that is physically hosted in the US East (N. Virginia) Region, us-east-1.
question: In which Region is the global AWS Organizations service hosted?

evidence.quote: AWS Organizations is a global service that is physically hosted in the US East (N. Virginia) Region (`us-east-1`).

claim: The per-entity policy attachment limits count only policies attached directly to an OU or account; policies that apply by inheritance do not count against them, and all policy attachment limits are hard limits.
question: Do inherited policies count against the attachment limits, and can the attachment limits be raised?

values.display: All policy limits are hard limits
values.spoken: all policy limits are hard limits

evidence.quote: These numbers apply to only those policies that are directly attached to an OU or an account. Policies that affect an OU or account by inheritance do ***not*** count against these limits. All policy limits are hard limits.
